Does Korea have 55+ community apartments like we do here?  My mother just moved into one of those apartments and it is God sent.  They have activity director that ensures something is going on every day (chili cook off, bingo, line dancing, pot luck ...) - and have all kinds of "groups" (knitting group, hiking group, jig saw puzzle group, any group).  So even elderlies without a family literally can have a group of people living right next to them to keep them company any day of the week.  It's a dorm style living except each dorm is like a luxury apartment.  They also have a theatre room, gym, pool, jacuzzi, "pub" ... where people can gather to socialize.  This is all in one building so it's very "cozy".   That type of living situation was not needed when I grew up there (I'm a Korean American), because people were expected to live with their sons when they got old.  But after watching your video, maybe it's time for Korea to introduce that type of living environment.

I went there in 2014. I was watching your videos in preparation before and during when I was there.  I was watching your early videos. The first year I was there, the teacher dinners were very drinking oriented. Even epik would talk about this and prepare you for it. The next year, we had dry dinners and hiking too! The next school I went to, there were younger teachers and the older middle aged principal wanted to drink but everyone just avoided him and went home. The smoking was intense everywhere but by 2015 there was more awareness and signs everywhere. People smoking in the bathrooms and fires starting. I remember always being asked to have kids... it was awkward. I think with the kids thing, many parents just let their kids go and be mischievous. If the children are not disciplined or managed by their parents, staff need to have awkward conversations to set. boundaries about noise and etc. I think customers are more argumentative these days and businesses don't want to deal with it.... kinda unfortunate...Eating out alone as mentioned was taboo and no seating arrangements. One of my coteachers and I were talking about living alone. She is was about early 40s and married. She had such fear about living alone like what if you died and no one else found you. I thought that was kinda extreme. But, I guess living alone abroad versus SK is different too. If you get sexually assaulted, you could have your abuser's family come and harass you. Pressing chargers was not as easy. She didn't understand about why anyone would wanna live alone. I liked this video. So much has changed the last 15 years.... more people are moving or visiting abroad ... more western individualism and realizing that toxic family or work dynamics don't need be tolerated......Basically, a generation with the internet with more information are opening up to newer ideas. The speed at which change and growth has happened in SK is faster than at the rate society can keep up with.

Being a mother is already so excruciatingly isolating. With more places becoming “child free” , it’s another reason on top of the thousand others to really think long and hard about taking on the immense burden of childcare. Can’t imagine being in the depths of PPD, finally getting out of the house with an infant or toddler to go get coffee, just trying to feel human, and getting turned away. This world was not built for women, whose biological reality often includes children. Children can only be taught how to behave through practice. But it seems like women are discouraged from even leaving the house with kids atp. They are both viewed as burdens instead of humans.

It seems like cultures are moving more towards putting your own feelings and emotions before others. While I think the opposite of this isn't good(only thinking about other people and not yourself), I think always putting yourself before others is part of what is causing the loneliness epidemic. I've even noticed in myself that I'm a lot less tolerant of people then I used to be 10 years ago, and part of that is due to putting my own happiness before others. Any kind of relationship is a partnership, and that means not only thinking of yourself but also of others. Hopefully the pendulum stops swinging so far from one extreme to the other and lands somewhere in the middle eventually.
